govt_response.title: Akashvani (News on AIR): MP CM declares state free of Naxalism after Maoist surrender in Balaghat (12 Dec 2025)
govt_response.summary: The state government's position is that coordinated central and state operations led to the surrender of the last two active cadres and that Balaghat now has no active hardcore Naxals.

analysis:
On 11 December 2025 two Naxalites surrendered at a CRPF camp in Balaghat. The Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister declared the state 'completely free from Naxal violence'. The Balaghat Superintendent of Police said no more hardcore Naxals were active in the district.

By the government's own account, the declaration rests on the surrender of the last two identified cadres, after 42 surrenders in the MP-Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh zone in 42 days. The MHA's national data show the number of Naxal-affected districts falling from 126 (2014) to 18 (2025).

There is no independent audit of the absence of Naxal activity, and the Chief Minister said the government would act to ensure the movement does not revive. Because 'Naxal-free' is a government self-assessment rather than a measured, independently verified outcome, the entry is recorded as unverifiable.
notes: The quote is a translation/paraphrase from PTI (ThePrint) and ANI; the original Hindi was not captured verbatim. The declared date of the surrender is 11 December 2025 (reported 12 December). I did not locate SATP or MHA district-level data confirming zero residual Naxal activity in Balaghat for 2026; a reviewer should check the latest MHA LWE-affected-district list for Madhya Pradesh.
